deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: inference-service v2.3.0 -> 10% in cluster-us-east-1 :rocket:
alert-bot: [ALERT] inference-service-canary - 5xx rate > 8% (last 1m) · triggered at 1765709020 · severity: P2
liam (oncall): paging oncall for P2: seeing 5xx on canary, grabbing logs now
sarah (engineer): i'm on terminal — checking pods, might be node-drain related, saw a node reboot during the rollout window earlier
liam (oncall): can you paste pod status?
sarah (engineer): ```kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep canary
inference-canary-5f7d4   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff   3   34m   10.2.7.45   node-12
inference-canary-6g8h1   1/1 Running           0   9m    10.2.7.60   node-14
```
sarah (engineer): node-12 shows "NotReady" earlier, someone had started a drain around 1765708950 but it didn't finish cleanly
liam (oncall): that lines up — crashloop on canary pod on the drained node. could be missing attached volume or improper preStop hook?
mike (sre): rolling drain can cause pod evictions landing on nodes without the right docker image if registry pulls fail. any image pull errors in pod events?
sarah (engineer): ```kubectl describe pod inference-canary-5f7d4 -n inference | tail -n 20
Events:
  Warning  Failed     3m (x4 over 4m)  kubelet, node-12  Error: ImagePullBackOff
  Normal   BackOff    2m (x5 over 3m)  kubelet, node-12  Back-off pulling image "redwood/inference:2.3.0-canary"
```
eva (product): customers on dedicated plans might hit higher latency if canary is bad and traffic doesn't failover — do we have traffic split?
liam (oncall): traffic is split 90/10 production/canary. we should flip feature flag to 100/0 for safety, then rollback canary. who can flip the flag?
sarah (engineer): I can toggle the rollout flag. doing 100% -> prod now.```curl -X POST https://featureflags.internal/api/toggles/inference_canary -d '{"percent":0}' -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx"```
sarah (engineer): flag set to 0% canary :white_check_mark: routing to stable only
alert-bot: [INFO] traffic change detected: inference-service canary traffic 0% at 1765709093
liam (oncall): good. now we should rollback the canary deployment and investigate node drain failure. Recommend: 1) rollback canary image -> previous stable 2) ensure node-12 is healthy/uncordoned 3) run drain with --delete-local-data --force? we need SRE input before force.
mike (sre): do not use --force yet. let's check node events and kubelet logs first. running: ```kubectl get node node-12 -o json | jq '.status.conditions[] | {type: .type, status: .status, reason: .reason}'```
mike (sre): node-12 kernel OOM killed kubelet yesterday, kubelet restarted but kube-proxy BGP flaps were seen. I'm going to cordon node-12 to stop new scheduling: `kubectl cordon node-12`
sarah (engineer): cordon done. also scaling down the canary ReplicaSet to 0 to stop crashloops: `kubectl scale rs inference-canary --replicas=0 -n inference`
liam (oncall): who will file the incident and notify customers? eva please coordinate customer comms saying partial canary rollout caused transient 5xx for a small percentage of traffic but failover occurred.
eva (product): drafting brief for impacted customers, will post to status page after we confirm rollback finished. ETA 15m
mike (sre): logs show image pull rate-limits from our registry for node-12's IP block — node-12 couldn't re-pull the canary image after drain. adding registry CIDR to allowed list for that node; also kicking off a controlled reboot of the node's kubelet: `sudo systemctl restart kubelet` (ops runbook step 4)
sarah (engineer): rollback executed: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-service --to-revision=12 -n inference`
alert-bot: [INFO] rollout undone for inference-service at 1765709158
liam (oncall): monitoring for 5xx regressions. please keep thread updated.
sarah (engineer): stable pods back up: ```kubectl get pods -n inference | grep inference-service
inference-service-abcde   3/3 Running   0   1m
```
mike (sre): node-12 kubelet restarted, node now Ready. I'll run a careful drain with `kubectl drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` after confirming no critical workloads remain.
liam (oncall): i'm going to hand off follow-up to mike (SRE) for root cause and long-term mitigation. oncall handover: 1765709220 -> handing to mike for postmortem, I'll update the incidents board.
mike (sre): taking over. next steps: collect kubelet logs, registry quota audit, ensure imagePullSecrets present in canary RS, and add retry/backoff and better pre-pull in rollout job.
eva (product): status page update posted: "Partial canary rollout caused errors for a small percentage of traffic; quick rollback completed; customers on dedicated plans saw transient errors. Investigating."
liam (oncall): closing active paging. if error recurs, page #oncall immediately. :v:
